fields.headline: COAST GUARD SAYS TSUNAMI THREAT PASSING
fields.lowerThird: Port Alder residents may begin returning home, Coast Guard spokesperson in Astoria tells Channel 8
fields.nameSuperTitle: Channel 8 Coast Bureau, reporting by phone
fields.ticker: Magnitude 8.0 earthquake struck off the Oregon coast at 10:14 a.m. • Highway 101 closed at the Alder River bridge in Port Alder • Highway 6 blocked by landslide on the Neskin grade • Cape Marlow PUD: power out countywide, no restoration time • Shelter open at Marlow Coast High School in Kellerton • Channel 8 News at 1:00: when can Port Alder go home?
fields.anchorBrief: Regional TV news frame: a reporter speaking by phone, shown as a still headshot over wide footage of a gray, rain-swept Oregon harbor with a calm-looking receding shoreline. Photographed at an angle off a small generator-powered TV in a crowded high school gym shelter.

instructorNote: This is misinformation. While the slide is up, read aloud the Channel 8 voicemail asking Dale to confirm a return time for the 1 o'clock news, the ARES report that people at the Spruce Hill aid station are packing up after seeing the clip on Starlink, and Position 2's report that its caller script still says M 8.0. Watch for the PIO to get the station to correct the chyron and to push one message on every channel (warning still in effect, larger waves possible, no return until Marlow County orders it). Also watch for the TWC and 911S to update the script and boards to M 9.0 (v3), and for Command to confirm the Coast Guard issued no return.

citations.quote: The NTWC cancels the warning. The Warning Coordinator, the Sheriff and the Harbor Master confirm waves are no longer observed (gauge readings at the Port Alder tide gauge below 0.3 meters of amplitude

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Press photograph, level horizon, 35 mm lens, sharp, natural daylight color. Wide aerial news-helicopter view of a small Oregon fishing harbor under heavy gray overcast at midday, steady rain streaking the frame. The water has pulled back unnaturally far, exposing wet mudflats, kelp-covered rocks and the bare pilings of wooden docks. Several plain white fishing boats rest tilted on the exposed seabed. Calm, glassy gray water sits far offshore beyond the breakwater. Dark evergreen hills rise behind a row of weathered waterfront buildings with flat unmarked rooftops and empty wet streets. Long telephoto lens, slightly compressed perspective, flat diffuse light, muted blue-gray palette, eerie quiet mood. Setting: on a coastal boardwalk with beachgoers looking at their phones, a tsunami evacuation route sign on a pole, calm sea beyond, daylight
